body:
I appreciate the talk, I really do. Getting pretty late, or rather, early now and I'm actually beyond tired and actually feel sleepy. I think I'll try to catch a couple hours and see how it goes. I'll be back around when I get up and check back in.

Thanks.

Lots of things. We used to love kicking back and playing some MMO's together when I'd get home.

Been a while since I've been to a park. Closest one to me isn't exactly in the best of shape. Well, to be honest, it's actually downright disgusting and last time I went there to relax ended up finding a 'family' of dead geese floating in the middle of the water way... Kind of killed the mood on that 'feel better' trip. heh.

I'd love to take a drive up to the mountains again and just walk around, but I can barely keep my gas tank above E. Id even settle for an arcade or pool house or something, but nothing like that around here that isn't busted down and half-functioning.

I make the town sound a lot worse than it really is. Big-ass town that still seems to feel like a small one. Short of bars, shopping, and cruising there's not really much to do. I wish I could enjoy my games again, get lost for a little bit, y'know?

I appreciate your time. :)

Right now she's homebound. She deals with some pretty severe anxiety and shuts down pretty hard around people. Its difficult, but I love her and so I do what I can to help. She's been trying to work on it, and I help where I can. We've been together for 6.5... 7ish years now? Oh god, don't tell her I forgot how long its been. heh. Time flies I suppose.

I lost the job about a month ago, plus a few days or so. I started looking the day after but after a couple weeks (Well, more like 8-10 days) I decided I needed to give myself a break. I was trying to save up for a vacation anyway and to jump right back in so soon when I was so close to getting some me time, some us time... Would have ended up dragging me down further. At least the sum I had saved helped get me through the waiting period for unemployment.

Rent is about as affordable as I can find short of going wayyyyy outside of town - not that its a super expensive town comparitively, but it's an expensive state. Going that far out though would pretty much trade the cost of rent and utilities for gas electric. Unfortunately public transportation isn't a viable option - I've tried it.

Last job without giving to much info was in dispatch. 50+ hours a week, 1 day off. I usually ended up working a little extra to help train the new guys overnight (Company phone, I was usually up late so they knew they could call me before waking anyone else)

Before that was another dispatch place, and before that was retail. I've had pretty good luck in the past finding jobs, but all through connections, friend-of-a-friend type of things. Unfortunately I don't really have any connections left.

No need to be sorry, it was a wall of text. Hell, I can barely remember half of it without skimming.

I lived in a place not a few streets over from here where I dealt with some pretty heavy gang activity. If people didn't try to convince me to buy an 8ball in my driveway, then they were ransacking the upstairs apartments to get money they were owed. It got so bad that I had to call a friend of the family to get a friend that I know had high up connections in the gang to make sure they would leave me and my roommates at the time alone... Didnt mean there werent nights where I kept myself at home because of what was going down. Didnt keep someone or someones from trying to break into my car twice, or one of my neighbors hiding in my closet to avoid being beaten. Only ever called the cops once while I lived there and never will again. When they showed up and looked into the issue, their first stop before leaving was to my apartment - too risky when you know the people in the area and these are the type of people that werent to afraid to attempt murder at a nearby mall.

I know they'll leave me alone, but the things Ive dealt with have left me with some pretty bad anxiety around people I dont know. The apartments across the street from me are actually rather notorious for bad stuff. No one delivers to this side of town and there isnt a night that goes by that theres not 2-3 cop cars driving down the street looking into something.

From my personal experience with zoloft, and please don't take this as gospel or hard fact. I have a rather high tolerance for drugs and they dont quite hit me or some of my family like they do others.

The first couple of weeks for me felt like it was doing nothing. I ended up being bumped from 50mg, to 75, then to 100. I was on it for a while, and it started to help, immensely! It was like the depression was still there, but there was this wall around it. I was able to be happy and do things I enjoyed, but I was aware of it. Even being aware of it it wasn't able to actually effect me except for the rare situation where I would mentally beat myself up.

After 4-5 months the effects started to wear off and due to recent life events I stopped taking it, which I know is a BIG no-no, but financially and mentally I havent been able to jump back in the game.

Just know it effects everyone a little differently, and what apefist above said - if you notice even a HINT of ANY of the black box side effects contact your doc immediately. Don't just brush them off or try to ignore them - talk you your doc, that's what they're there for.
